skills.trigger: When evaluating sequential chest X-rays showing rapidly evolving bilateral opacities with significant resolution over a short period (e.g., days).
steps: Compare the extent and density of bilateral alveolar opacities across the time-series images to confirm rapid onset and subsequent clearing.
Assess the cardiac silhouette size; normal heart size supports non-cardiogenic edema (like ARDS) over cardiogenic pulmonary edema.
Distinguish from pneumonia by noting that bacterial consolidation typically resolves much slower than the observed rapid clearance.
Correlate the imaging pattern of diffuse alveolar damage with rapid resolution to supportive care/ventilation rather than specific antimicrobial or diuretic therapy.
